title: GP Québec and Montréal 2026 preview: Canada one-day race routes, favourites and how to watch
content:

GP Québec and Montréal 2026 preview: Canada one-day race routes, favourites and how to watch

Grand Tour season is almost over with the Vuelta a España racing towards its conclusion, but the autumn Classics are kicking into gear with the two Canadian one-day races of GP Québec and Montréal, which will take place on 11th and 13th September respectively.

The races take place on tough city circuits with the opener in Québec City more suited to sprinters and puncheurs and the Montréal race suiting climbers with an extra 2,000m of race altitude.

This year’s GP Montréal takes on extra significance as the 2026 World Championships will take place in Montréal on a similar route at the end of September, so many riders will be hoping to use it as a practice run – especially with the race for the rainbow jersey wide open after Tadej Pogačar’s season-ending Vuelta crash.

In 2025 Québec was won by Julian Alaphilippe ahead of Pavel Sivakov and Alberto Bettiol, and with Alaphilippe’s retirement and Sivakov at the Vuelta, only Bettiol will return from that podium. While the course is generally more suited to versatile sprinters, there aren’t a whole lot of them on this year’s start list, so three-time winner Michael Matthews looks well suited for a fourth victory, but he’ll face competition from the likes of Kaden Groves, Corbin Strong and Luke Lamperti.

However a solo or small group finish can’t be ruled out, and contenders for both Québec and Montréal, which have the same start list, include big-time climbing talents such as Isaac del Toro, Remco Evenepoel, Paul Seixas, Matteo Jorgenson and newly crowned MTB XCO World Champion Tom Pidcock, plus Classics hitters like Jhonatan Narváez, Florian Vermeersch, Tim Wellens, Louis Barré, Tiesj Benoot, Quinn Simmons, Alec Segaert, Mauro Schmid, Ben Healy and Jenno Berckmoes.

GP Québec and Montréal 2026 key information

  • Dates: Québec – Friday 11th September; Montréal – Sunday 13th September 2026
  • Distances: 206km (20 laps); 214.4km (16 laps)
  • Elevation gain: 2,780m; 4,304m
  • Television coverage: TNT Sports, HBO Max, TVA Sports, CBC GEM, Eurosport, L’Equipe, FloBikes
  • 2025 winners: Julian Alaphilippe (Tudor); Brandon McNulty (UAE Team Emirates XRG)

GP Québec 2026 route

In Québec, riders take on 20 laps of a 10.3km circuit, with the headline being almost 2km of climbing at the end with the Côte de la Montagne (600m, 9% average, 13% max), which goes straight into the Montée rue Saint-Louis (1km, 3%).

There’s only 139m elevation gain per lap, but it adds up to 2,780, so it’s no walk in the park.

GP Montréal 2026 route

The Montréal circuit is a proper Classic, and very tough, with a total elevation gain over 4,300m, so it’s no surprise Pogačar normally dominates here and was seen as a shoo-in for this year’s Worlds road race before his crash.

There’s barely a flat metre of the 13.4km circuit, which is taken on 16 times for a total distance of 214.4km, with four climbs, which get smaller as the lap progresses.

Pretty much straight out of the gate riders go up the Voie Camillien-Houde (1.8km, 8% average), then it’s the Chemin de Polyechnique (780m, 6% average – including 200m at 11%), followed by the Avenue Pagnuelo (534m, 7.5% average), before the last punch up the Avenue du Parc (600m, 4% average) for a slight uphill finish to the race.

With no Pogačar to dictate, how this goes is anyone’s game. Can Isaac del Toro replicate his teammate’s success? Will Remco Evenepoel take advantage of the Slovenian’s absence? Will Paul Seixas set himself up for a rainbow jersey tilt? Will Tom Pidcock carry his MTB form across the Atlantic? It should be a thriller.

GP Québec 2026 favourites

Three-time champ Michael Matthews will fancy his chances of making it a fourth GP Québec victory, with a weaker sprint field than normal – his main competitors if it comes to a bunch finish being Kaden Groves and Corbin Strong. Last year it came down to a breakaway trio though, so the don’t rule out punchier riders and even a big name climber to go clear, with plenty of uphill kilometres on the course. A long Remco Evenepoel solo is always on the cards in a hilly Classics, especially with no Pogačar.

Cyclist‘s favourites

★★★★★: Michael Matthews (Jayco AlUla)
★★★★: Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Jhonatan Narvaez (UAE Team Emirates XRG), Kaden Groves (Alpecin-Premier Tech)
★★★: Isaac del Toro (UAE Team Emirates XRG), Tom Pidcock (Pinarello Q36.5), Quinn Simmons (Lidl-Trek)
★★: Jenno Berckmoes (Lotto Intermarche), Corbin Strong (NSN), Tim Wellens (UAE Team Emirates XRG)
★: Luke Lamperti (EF Education-EasyPost), Edoardo Zambanini (Bahrain Victorious), Alec Segaert (Bahrain Victorious), Alberto Bettiol (XDS Astana)

GP Montréal 2026 favourites

Pogačar has controlled GP Montréal over the last few years, gifting his teammate Brandon McNulty the victory in 2025. Although the Slovenian isn’t there this year, the start list is more stacked than ever thanks to the draw of the World Championships in a couple of weeks time. With that in mind, this should come down to a properly big name rider like Evenepoel, Isaac del Toro, Paul Seixas or Tom Pidcock. Others are certainly possible, especially given Quinn Simmons’ climbing form, but it would be a surprise.

Cyclist‘s favourites

★★★★★: Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe)
★★★★: Isaac del Toro (UAE Team Emirates XRG), Paul Seixas (Decathlon CMA CGM), Tom Pidcock (Pinarello Q36.5)
★★★: Giulio Ciccone (Lidl-Trek), Quinn Simmons (Lidl-Trek), Louis Barré (Visma-Lease a Bike), Michael Matthews (Jayco-AlUla)

How to watch GP Québec and Montréal 2026

The 2026 GP Québec and Montréal will be available to watch on TNT Sports and HBO Max in the UK, Eurosport in Europe, HBO Max in the US, FloBikes in Australia and New Zealand, and TVA Sports and CBC GEM in Canada.

  • Belgium: Pickx
  • Canada: TVA Sports, CBC GEM
  • Europe: Eurosport, HBO Max
  • France: L’Équipe
  • Luxembourg: Pickx
  • Oceania: FloBikes
  • United Kingdom: TNT Sports, HBO Max
  • United States: HBO Max
